name: Intelius

steps.note: On verified_on this address redirected to a suppression centre on another host, which is the page captured here and the page the rest of these steps describe. Intelius' own search box was not captured, so search_url_template is the site's front page and a scan types into the box there the way a person would. Whether the person is listed cannot be settled that way: on 2026-09-09 every search on Intelius led into a page that sells a report rather than a free result, so the scan records not_assessable for this broker and says why. A name-directory page is the likely door and this manifest has no name_page block, because no capture of the directory path exists yet.

The one box in Step 1. The page says a verification email with a link to carry on is sent to it, so it has to be an inbox the person can open, and it says the address is used only to facilitate and process the request.

steps.prompt: The email address is in the box and nothing has been sent. One box is still unticked, and it agrees to the site's terms of use and privacy policy and consents to transactional email about the suppression tool. Agreeing to terms is yours to do, not mine. Check the address, read those two documents if you want to, then say yes and I will tick the box and press Continue.

selector.label: I agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy, and consent to receive transactional emails regarding my use of the Suppression Tool.

steps.note: Ticked only after the gate above, because agreeing to terms is the person's to do.

steps.prompt: A verification email with a link is on its way to that address. Everything after Step 1 sits behind that link, so open it and carry on in the browser yourself. What you are heading for is a screen called Control: it shows the identity the site has matched to that address, and a Desired Behavior dropdown. Setting that to Suppressed and pressing Save is the thing that actually suppresses the report. Read what the screen says the report is currently set to before you change anything, because an account that already exists is not a suppression. The run this capture comes from found an identity that already carried a date of birth, and the report was still set to displayed, which is the one line on that frame you can read for yourself. One suppression covers four sites, which the page names. Tell me what each screen asked for and say when Save has gone through.
steps.note: This is where the manifest stops and the flow does not. Nothing has been suppressed at this point; an address has been given and a link asked for. The Control screen is captured and described here from that capture, but no step reaches it: it sits behind a link sent to a verified address, and nothing in this schema can say that a flow resumes in a later sitting from a link only the person can open. See notes.

verification.success_when: A search by name on Intelius no longer returns a background report for the person. The page is explicit that this is what suppression covers and no more: it applies to the report a name search generates on the sites it names, and it says the name may still appear in phone, address, or email reports found by those criteria, that other sources are unaffected, and that data held about the person as a user of those sites is a separate matter.

additional_captures.of: The page's own answers to what the suppression tool does and what it costs, on the same visit, with the fine print under them in the same frame. It is where the four covered sites are named and where the limits on that coverage are stated

The Control screen, from a real run on 2026-09-10 rather than a fresh visit, because nobody reaches it without a verified email address. One solid box covers the whole identity block: record id, name, date of birth, and two aliases. No address appears in that block, though the run testimony records that the record was filed under an old one. What is left is the sentence saying the report is currently configured as displayed, and the Desired Behavior control that changes it

id_requirements.note: Step 1 asks for an email address and nothing else, and the page states the tool is free. What it does require is control of an email address the record already carries, proved by clicking a link sent to it. That is a different kind of requirement from a document and is not an id_requirement as this schema means the term. The page also names a separate route by email for judges, law enforcement officers and other legally protected people, which asks for a full name, date of birth, city and state of residence, phone number and email address. That paragraph is on the coverage capture, above the two answers the syndication note cites. That is a different process from this one and no step here uses it.

notes: Written from three frames: two of the suppression page captured fresh on verified_on, and the Control screen from a real run with its identity block under a solid box. Intelius' own opt-out address redirects to a PeopleConnect Suppression Center on another host, and that is the page every step here describes. What this broker actually is, because the old manifest called it a form and it is not one. It is an account. The person proves control of an email address the record already carries, follows a link, and arrives at a screen called Control whose Desired Behavior dropdown sets the background report to suppressed. No form is filled with a name or an address anywhere in it. Step 1 is the only part a manifest can drive, and this one drives exactly that and stops. An existing account is not a suppression. The run of 2026-09-10 found an identity that already held a date of birth, filed under an address the person had moved from, while the report was still set to displayed. Only the displayed half of that is legible on the capture; the rest is under the box and is recorded here as run testimony rather than as something the image shows. Somebody who opened an account in the past and assumes they are covered is not. That is why the handoff asks the person to read what the report is set to before changing anything. SYNDICATION NOTE, and this catalogue's first. The page states in its own words, under the heading asking what the suppression tool does, that it manages the display of the background report on all people search sites in the PeopleConnect family including TruthFinder.com, InstantCheckmate.com, Intelius.com and USSearch.com. One suppression therefore covers four sites. That sentence is legible on captures/intelius-suppression-coverage.jpg, which is the only reason this note exists; no relationship is recorded anywhere in this catalogue on any other basis. The same frame carries the limits, and they belong in the same breath as the claim. The tool covers the Public Data a name search generates and not the User Data those sites hold about their own customers. It does not reach other PeopleConnect sites, and the page names Classmates.com as one it does not reach. It does not affect the third-party sources the data came from. And a name may still surface through phone, address, or email searches, or on registered sex offender lists. A four-site coverage claim without those limits beside it would be the broker's marketing rather than its terms. What the schema cannot say here, recorded rather than worked around. There is no way to describe a broker whose opt-out is an account: no step type for proving control of an address, none for a session that resumes from an emailed link in a later sitting, and no way to say that a setting rather than a submission is the act that matters. method is form because that is the closest value the enum offers and there is no honest one. The suppression itself is therefore a handoff, described from a capture but not driven. Inventing a step type from one broker would be guessing at a category from a single example, so the gap is written down here and in step-types.md and left open. It states no processing window anywhere, so recheck_after_days is null with recheck_stated false and the wait is the orchestrator's own. Exposure cannot be assessed from this broker's search: a scan on 2026-09-09 found every search route into a report-selling funnel with no free result list, which is not_assessable rather than not_found. That is recorded from the scan and not from a capture. The fix is a name-directory page, and there is no name_page block here because the directory path has not been captured; a pattern noticed in a live search is a lead, not provenance. What the captures show and what they do not: Step 1's heading, its field label, the consent sentence, the privacy line and the Continue button are on the first frame; the coverage and cost answers and the fine print are on the second; the displayed sentence and the Desired Behavior control are on the third. Selectors carry no css fallbacks, because this host's markup was not read. No image holds a browser address bar, so optout_url records the address that was typed and source_url the address it redirected to. home_url and search_url_template are the brand's own front page, which the second frame names in the list of covered sites. Two captures from that run are not here and will not be. Steps 7 and 8 show a verification code and an email address, and neither is repo material in any form.
